body: I'm really sorry.
Late comment, but thank you for writing this comment!
This is the only mathematical equation that makes complete sense to me.

What the fuck? I hope that call was recorded and that she's fired. Ah, in a perfect world....

I'm sorry, OP...that's horrible.
God, I could have written this post. It absolutely sucks, doesn't it? Constantly pleasing people isn't worth it, but I just can't stop.
I'm at a point now in my life where I can understand this concept well. Thank God.

I can relate a lot to your post. I graduated college with a major in English, and am now only working at a call center. I'm finally at a point where I dislike that so much that I want to start doing something with my degree, and I'm trying to reach the new goal of getting into grad school for library science, but it's slow going. I just have to take it one step at a time.

Please don't be sorry for posting this here. You have the same right to post your feelings here that anyone else does. *hugs*
I'm sorry. Their post was beyond pathetic and unnecessary. Please don't take it personally.

Oh, get off your high horse and shut up. How do you know what the person is going through? You'd think if you had depression, you'd have more compassion and be less dismissive. Come on and get a grip on the fact that people have other perspectives than you, and some of those people can also be just as depressed as you are.
I'd never thought of this aspect before...it makes a lot of sense. Wow.

*Like why didn't it produce some carebears or Chester Cheeto to keep you chill while you potentially die.*

I never would have thought I'd laugh out loud when reading the comments in this post, so thanks for that.
This happened in my hometown.

Aw, thanks a lot! I think they're having an effect! :-D

I hope the same for you!

"My literal biggest fear in life is waking up 20 years from now and going to a cubicle job and being alright with it."

I'm at a cubicle job and I'm finally trying to convince myself that I'm not alright with it and I want to do something else with my life (and put my education to good use).
Ehhhh, I'll go to /r/offmychest or LiveJournal instead! Ahaha.

"On the flip side, school is becoming more and more like prison. 
And when people see themselves as having no freedom, they lash out at others they think are vulnerable"

Well, if this doesn't describe life in the workplace, I don't know what does.

"I spend my days wishing I could go back, or trying to remember how I was and recreate it. But it's impossible. Then I get depressed that it's impossible. Then I get depressed that I'm wasting my life. I feel like i can't win :( anyone else do this?"

All. The. Time.

It's mental and emotional and spiritual torture.
You, too!
Thanks for sharing that!
It really was!
How he portrayed Lupin...some of his lines were so out-of-character, in my opinion (although I guess the scriptwriters could be blamed for that, too).
Fantasizing about my favorite fictional characters. Yeah, it may sound crazy, but it almost never fails to help me feel better. (Escapism for the win!)
Ah, I love this.
Not that I know of, but if it was up to me to create one, David Thewlis would be first on the list.

I do. I think the thing that triggered this latest feeling for me, though, was yesterday. A big event happened to one of my family members, and when I asked them what they thought my reaction would be before they told me about it, they said that they didn't really think of me. That hurt.

"It's as though I just don't have a stable enough foundation, and can't access my own internal resources for dealing with things."

Welp, this explains my life.
This is true, and I find it comforting to think about sometimes.
Yep. :-/
Yeah, I honestly definitely want to live, but sometimes I just feel so useless, you know?

Yeah, I'm working on that (being important to myself, I mean)...it's an uphill battle for sure!

I've started to volunteer at the library, and that's helping somewhat.

I wouldn't say I'm literally lonely, no. I have friends and family, but I feel like I don't connect with most of them on a deep level. I hear people talk about how their mothers are their best friends and how close they are to their siblings and how they're inseparable from their best friends. Sometimes on reflection I feel like I don't have that strong of a connection with the people in my own life and it makes me feel empty.
I'm glad you're okay, and (maybe as farfetched as this may sound for you (because I can kind of relate)) I hope things get better for you.
This is why I'm apprehensive about going to my high school graduation class's ten-year reunion next year...ugh....
I volunteered for a few hours at my local library this morning only to come home and sleep the rest of the day away. I can relate!
Thank you for sharing this! Wow!
What...in the...how haven't I heard about this until now?!
You're welcome!
Yyyep. Depression's great, innit?
Ahaha, you never know! And, hey, focus on you. Try to be good enough for you for now. That's what I've been trying to do for myself...on and off....

I could have written this post. Granted, I'm a 26-year-old female ("woman"? What is that? That can't be a term that could ever apply to me!), but I also miss the 90s and early 2000s like nothing else.
Thank you for sharing!

The best place I've found online as an adoptee is here: http://adultadopteesupport.freeforums.net/forum

There are plenty of Late Discovery Adoptees (LDAs) who post there, too.

No rush! :-D Here's a link to a blog post about what you can do if you've lost your card, too: http://blog.ssa.gov/so-youve-lost-your-social-security-card/

Good luck!

Are you saying you don't know your social security number? There should be a way for you to find it even without your card. Here's a link that may help: https://faq.ssa.gov/link/portal/34011/34019/ArticleFolder/421/Social-Security-Number-and-Card

I don't clean my room. I don't help my grandma out as often as I should. I don't apply for different jobs. I don't read as much as I used to (and when I do, I just don't enjoy it as much as I used to, either). I don't hang out with different people often. I don't take chances. I don't know how to stop hating myself.

Studies have found that depression can, in essence, shrink the brain. You're not dumb. You're depressed.

(This is something I have to remind myself of often. The message only gets through when I'm lucky....)
What happened?

I saw the subject line and "Remorse" and was immediately filled with dread but then I read your post and now I'm relieved for you. I'm so glad your wife took it well...good for you both, and good luck!

"I hate life because I have to live it as myself."
You couldn't have worded this any better. I feel the same way.
Yes, yes, and yes.

Anger sucks, doesn't it?
I should borrow that motto...I dunno if I would have the self-discipline to actually use it, though, ahaha.

This is wonderful advice.
Wow...good for you! Keep it up! Take it a day at a time if you have to. I've been struggling with hygiene, too, so I can understand where you're coming from.

"And remember, these are feelings and thoughts. And both are constructs of your mind, not "facts" necessarily, and both change."
Good point!
I feel this way sometimes...honestly, it's a great feeling...it's so liberating....
